certification.note: the probe certifies mass/momentum conservation at the declared certification_horizon and reports the whole horizon table plus the measured per-step defect, because a linearly accumulating defect makes the horizon part of the claim

provenance.note: the backend package is imported by file location under the declared repo, and the resolved module_file/sha256 is stored with the residual; a module resolved outside the declared repo raises ProvenanceError so the residual is WITHHELD. Reason (measured 2026-11-10): an unpinned `import tensorlbm` on a shared host resolved to another agent's worktree while the artifact recorded this repo's commit -> mass defect 9.3e-7 attributed to a checkout whose kernel actually conserves to 1.1e-16.

purpose: Kernel conservation probe. Reading residuals out of finished artifacts only tells you what a past run happened to record; this probe *measures* mass and momentum conservation for an actual solver kernel on a problem whose exact answer is known (periodic domain, uniform equilibrium, no walls: streaming is a permutation and the collision operator must conserve mass and momentum exactly up to working precision). The probe is what makes the C2 residual claim measurable rather than quotable.

residual_definitions.energy: not defined for an isothermal model: the D2Q9 collision has no energy equation, so no energy-conservation claim is made
residual_definitions.mass: |sum(rho_N) - sum(rho_0)| / sum(rho_0) over the whole periodic box
residual_definitions.momentum: |P_x(N) - P_x(0)| / |P_x(0)| with P_x = sum(rho u_x); the y-component is reported separately as an absolute value because its reference magnitude vanishes
